title: Restore Valid IP Addresses
statement: A logging system stripped all the dots out of IPv4 addresses, leaving only the raw digit strings. Given a string digits containing only characters '0'-'9', reconstruct every valid IPv4 address that could have produced it by inserting exactly three dots (splitting the string into exactly four segments that together use every character, in order). A segment is valid when it is 1 to 3 characters long, its numeric value is between 0 and 255 inclusive, and it has no leading zero (a segment starting with '0' is only valid if it is exactly "0"). Return the reconstructed addresses as a list of strings sorted in ascending lexicographic (string) order. If no valid address can be formed — including when the string is shorter than 4 or longer than 12 characters — return an empty list.
hints: You must split the string into exactly four parts, each 1-3 characters. How would you try every way of placing the three dots and abandon a partial split as soon as a segment is invalid?

Backtrack on (start index, segments chosen so far): at each step try segment lengths 1, 2, 3 from start, keep the segment only if it passes the 0-255 and leading-zero checks, and prune when the remaining characters can no longer fit in the remaining segments (fewer than 1 or more than 3 per segment).

A segment is valid iff int(seg) <= 255 AND (len(seg) == 1 or seg[0] != '0'). Recurse: when 4 segments are chosen and start == len(digits), join them with dots and record; after the recursive call, pop the segment to un-choose. Sort the collected strings before returning.
